title: An Ii-Key-containing HPV16/18 E7 epitope peptide vaccine promotes dendritic cell activation and T-cell immunity in a murine HPV16 tumor model, with greater tumor control upon PD-1 blockade.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Background Therapeutic vaccines targeting human papillomavirus (HPV) E6/E7 oncoproteins represent a promising strategy for cervical cancer immunotherapy, yet most candidates remain constrained by insufficient antigen presentation efficiency and suboptimal T-cell responses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The Ii-Key strategy, which links the invariant chain (Ii) core motif to epitope peptides to facilitate MHC class II loading, may overcome this limitation by amplifying CD4 + T helper responses. HPV16/18 E7 epitopes restricted by murine H-2 class I/II molecules were predicted using immunoinformatics tools. In vivo immunogenicity was assessed in C57BL/6 mice through immune phenotyping of lymphoid organs and plasma cytokine profiling.
analysis.methods: Ii-Key-modified MHC class II peptides (LRMK-PEG2-epitope) and unmodified MHC class I peptides were synthesized and evaluated in vitro using bone marrow-derived dendritic cell (BMDC) stimulation assays with flow cytometry, ELISA, and western blotting. Anti-tumor activity was tested in an early-intervention subcutaneous TC-1 tumor model (HPV16 E6/E7-positive) with histopathological and flow cytometric analyses of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes.
analysis.main_results: The peptide pool promoted BMDC maturation, as evidenced by increased frequencies of CD80 + CD86 + and I-A/I-E + BMDCs, NF-κB pathway activation, and increased proinflammatory cytokine secretion; these readouts indicate DC activation. In the TC-1 model, peptide treatment suppressed tumor growth and qualitatively reduced tumor Ki67 staining, accompanied by non-significant trends toward increased intratumoral CD4 + and CD8 + T-cell frequencies.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The Ii-Key-containing HPV16/18 E7 peptide formulation promoted dendritic cell activation and T-cell immunity, achieving anti-tumor activity in an early-intervention TC-1 model with acceptable tolerability. Combination with anti-PD-1 produced greater tumor control than either monotherapy; this comparison does not establish additivity or synergy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These preclinical findings support further evaluation of the formulation incorporating direct antigen-presentation assays and matched unmodified MHC-II peptide controls. The results suggest potential for improving therapeutic vaccines against HPV-associated cancers by enhancing antigen presentation and T-cell responses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Safety assessments by histopathology and serum biochemistry indicated acceptable tolerability under the conditions and observation period tested. The supplied evidence does not report long-term safety or efficacy data, nor does it provide information on human trials or broader applicability to other HPV types.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential of an Ii-Key-containing HPV16/18 E7 epitope peptide vaccine to promote dendritic cell activation and T-cell immunity in a murine HPV16 tumor model. The research aimed to address the limitations of current therapeutic vaccines, which often suffer from poor antigen presentation and suboptimal T-cell responses. The study design involved in vitro and in vivo assessments using immunoinformatics tools, BMDC stimulation assays, and a TC-1 tumor model. The main results showed that the vaccine formulation enhanced dendritic cell maturation and activated T-cell responses, leading to tumor suppression. The combination of the vaccine with anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody demonstrated greater tumor control than either treatment alone. The findings suggest that this approach could improve therapeutic vaccines against HPV-associated cancers, but the study lacks long-term safety data and human trial information, limiting the strength of the evidence.

title: Neoepitope-based cancer vaccines in human papillomavirus–negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a review

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the use of neoepitope-based cancer vaccines in human papillomavirus (HPV)-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). The central question is whether these vaccines can improve outcomes in HPV-negative HNSCC, given the substantial risk of recurrence despite multimodal treatment.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature, with a specific emphasis on the TG4050 randomized phase I study in 33 patients with resected HPV-negative HNSCC. The study supports the feasibility and immunogenicity of personalized neoepitope vaccination but lacks sufficient data to draw definitive efficacy conclusions due to its small sample size, few recurrence events, and per-protocol analysis. The review also highlights the need for adequately powered randomized trials to establish the clinical role of neoepitope vaccination in HPV-negative HNSCC.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that mutation-derived neoepitopes offer a rationale for personalized vaccination in HPV-negative HNSCC, but their clinical relevance depends on factors such as target expression, clonality, antigen presentation, and T-cell functionality. It also emphasizes that while complementary translational and cross-tumor studies provide insights into antigen selection, vaccine delivery, and combination strategies, their transferability to HPV-negative HNSCC remains uncertain.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is limited evidence on the efficacy of neoepitope-based vaccines in HPV-negative HNSCC, with the TG4050 study being too small to provide conclusive results. Additionally, the review notes that the roles of spatial immune profiling and circulating tumor DNA in guiding vaccination are still exploratory. The review also highlights the need for more research on the treatment setting, the added benefit of vaccination to standard therapies, and the connection between immune measurements and clinical outcomes.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future studies should define the treatment setting, evaluate whether vaccination adds benefit to contemporary standard treatment, report manufacturing attrition and time to first dose, and connect standardized immune measurements with clinical outcomes. The review also suggests that spatial immune profiling and circulating tumor DNA monitoring could be valuable tools in understanding resistance and disease progression, though their roles in guiding vaccination remain under investigation.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the potential of neoepitope-based cancer vaccines in HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), a condition with high recurrence rates despite multimodal treatment. It highlights the rationale for personalized vaccination based on mutation-derived neoepitopes, but notes that clinical relevance depends on factors like target expression, clonality, antigen presentation, and T-cell functionality. The narrative review distinguishes direct evidence on HPV-negative HNSCC from broader HNSCC programs and cross-tumor studies. The TG4050 phase I study supports feasibility and immunogenicity but lacks power to determine efficacy due to its small size and few recurrence events. The review underscores the need for adequately powered trials and emphasizes the importance of defining treatment settings, evaluating vaccine benefits in combination with standard therapies, and linking immune measurements to clinical outcomes. It also suggests that spatial immune profiling and circulating tumor DNA monitoring may offer insights into resistance and disease progression, though their roles in guiding vaccination remain exploratory.

title: Vaginal Intraepithelial Neoplasia: HPV16 and Grade as Recurrence Predictors in a 10-Year Series.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize the clinical profile, treatment patterns and factors associated with high-grade recurrence in patients with vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VaIN) over a 10-year period.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective single-center cohort study was conducted from 2013 to 2023, including 71 consecutive patients with histologically confirmed VaIN.
analysis.methods: The primary outcome was histologically confirmed high-grade recurrence or progression (HSIL+: VaIN2–3 or invasive carcinoma), with VaIN1 on follow-up not considered recurrence. The study analyzed HPV genotypes and their association with recurrence outcomes.
analysis.main_results: The mean age was 47.9±10.5 years. Index grades were VaIN1/LSIL in 59.2%, VaIN2 in 32.4%, and VaIN3 in 8.5%. High-risk HPV was detected in 71.8% of patients, with HPV16 identified in 22.5% and 52.8% having multiple infections.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that HPV16-positive patients had shorter HSIL+-free survival, although the crude difference in HSIL+ rates was not statistically significant. Index HSIL showed a non-significant trend towards higher recurrence.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that HPV16 and the initial grade of VaIN may be important factors in predicting high-grade recurrence, which could inform more targeted surveillance strategies for HPV-associated diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by a small number of events (12) and a non-significant trend in some results, which may affect the strength of the conclusions. However, the hypothesis-generating nature of the findings supports further prospective evaluation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the clinical profile, treatment patterns, and recurrence predictors in patients with vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VaIN) over a 10-year period at a tertiary referral center. The primary outcome was high-grade recurrence or progression, defined as HSIL+ (VaIN2–3 or invasive carcinoma). The study found that HPV16 positivity was associated with earlier recurrence, although the difference was not statistically significant. Index HSIL showed a non-significant trend towards higher recurrence. The mean age of participants was 47.9±10.5 years, with the majority having VaIN1/LSIL. High-risk HPV was detected in 71.8% of patients, and 52.8% had multiple infections. These hypothesis-generating findings, limited by a small number of events, suggest the need for prospective evaluation of genotype- and grade-based surveillance strategies for HPV-associated diseases.

title: HPV Infection in Sub-Saharan Africa: Circulating Genotypes, Vaccination Strategies (Single-Dose Versus Two-Dose), and Implications of HIV Co-Infection

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on human papillomaviruses (HPV), specifically examining circulating genotypes, vaccination strategies (single-dose versus two-dose), and the implications of HIV co-infection in sub-Saharan Africa. The central question is whether single-dose vaccination is as effective as two-dose regimens in preventing HPV-related diseases, particularly in immunocompetent populations and those living with HIV.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing evidence, drawing on randomized trials conducted in Tanzania, Kenya, and Costa Rica. It includes studies on HPV genotype distribution, vaccine efficacy, and immunogenicity. The review does not report on meta-analysis or pooled estimates but relies on direct comparisons and observational data.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HPV 16 and HPV 18 remain the predominant oncogenic types in sub-Saharan Africa, although other high-risk types such as HPV 35, HPV 52, HPV 45, HPV 33, and HPV 58 are also frequently reported. Single-dose vaccination has demonstrated durable immunogenicity and high efficacy against persistent vaccine-type infections, with evidence from trials in Tanzania and Kenya showing efficacy above 98% over 54 months. A Costa Rican trial also found non-inferiority of one dose compared to two doses over five years.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is a lack of direct evidence on the efficacy and durability of single-dose HPV vaccination in people living with HIV. While immunogenicity and efficacy data are available for immunocompetent populations, these findings cannot be directly transferred to HIV-positive individuals due to the absence of target-specific studies. Additionally, some high-risk HPV infections fall outside the coverage of bivalent and quadrivalent vaccines, and certain types remain outside nonavalent vaccine coverage.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest that single-dose vaccination should be expanded in immunocompetent populations, while multidose vaccination pathways should be maintained for people living with HIV. There is a need for genotype-specific surveillance and continued cervical screening to address the gaps in vaccine coverage and to monitor the effectiveness of vaccination strategies in the region.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the role of human papillomaviruses (HPV) in sub-Saharan Africa, focusing on circulating genotypes, vaccination strategies, and the impact of HIV co-infection. It highlights that HPV 16 and HPV 18 are the most prevalent oncogenic types, though other high-risk variants are also common. Single-dose vaccination has shown high efficacy and durability in immunocompetent populations, supported by trials in Tanzania, Kenya, and Costa Rica. However, evidence for single-dose efficacy in people living with HIV is lacking. The review recommends expanded single-dose vaccination alongside multidose pathways for HIV-positive individuals, genotype-specific surveillance, and continued cervical screening to address gaps in vaccine coverage and improve public health outcomes.

title: The Association of Oral and Anogenital Human Papillomavirus Genotypes With Head and Neck Cancers in Brazil: A Nationwide Case-Control Study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the association of oral and anogenital human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes with head and neck cancers in Brazil, addressing the need to understand the role of HPV in these cancers.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A nationwide case-control study conducted between 2019 and 2023, involving 314 participants (157 cases and 157 controls), mostly males aged 50–65 years.
analysis.methods: Oral, genital, and anal samples were collected and processed at a central laboratory for HPV genotyping, and associations were estimated using conditional regression.
analysis.main_results: Oral HPV prevalence was similar between cases and controls (14% vs. 12%), with HPV-16/18 more prevalent among cases (7.3% vs. Genital HPV prevalence was 39% with no case–control differences, while anal HPV prevalence was 17%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that oral HPV-16/18 infection was independently associated with head and neck cancer, especially oropharyngeal carcinoma, highlighting its potential role in this disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that oral HPV-16/18 may be a significant risk factor for head and neck cancers, particularly oropharyngeal carcinoma, which could inform targeted screening and prevention strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study had a relatively small sample size and relied on self-reported data, which may limit generalizability. However, the evidence is strong due to the use of a matched case-control design and central laboratory processing.

analysis.summary_en: This nationwide case-control study in Brazil investigated the association of oral and anogenital human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes with head and neck cancers. The study included 314 participants, mostly males aged 50–65 years, and found that oral HPV-16/18 infection was independently associated with head and neck cancer, particularly oropharyngeal carcinoma. Genital HPV prevalence was 39%, and anal HPV prevalence was 17%, with no significant case–control differences observed for genital HPV. The study highlights the potential role of oral HPV-16/18 in head and neck cancers, which could inform targeted screening and prevention strategies. However, the study's small sample size and reliance on self-reported data may limit its generalizability, though the evidence is considered strong due to the matched case-control design and central laboratory processing.

title: Social Media Insights Into the Human Papillomavirus Vaccination Catch-Up Campaign for Young Adults in the Netherlands, 2023-2024: Qualitative Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination prevents HPV-related cancers, but its uptake remains suboptimal. As young adults increasingly seek health information online, understanding online questions, concerns, and misinformation in response to the campaign may help improve future vaccination efforts.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In the Netherlands, a catch-up campaign invited individuals aged 18 to 27 years for an additional cost-free opportunity to initiate or complete their HPV vaccination in 2023‐2024, which led to 24% of the invited population getting vaccinated.
analysis.methods: Following an inventory of potential platforms and data sources, a retrospective online social listening analysis was conducted across Instagram, Facebook, and X (formerly Twitter), using data from PHS Amsterdam, the National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, the Dutch public broadcasting foundation, and LINDA.meiden from January 1, 2023, to June 1, 2024. Publicly available posts, comments, and engagement concerning HPV vaccination were manually collected and inductively coded.
analysis.main_results: A total of 821 posts and 5157 comments were collected and analyzed. Ten recurring themes were identified across varying risk levels. Two themes were classified as high risk: an information gap regarding HPV vaccination effectiveness and concerns about the transparency regarding HPV vaccine side effects. Three themes were classified as medium risk: questioning HPV vaccine effectiveness, reduced general vaccine trust following COVID-19, and accessibility issues related to vaccination locations and service times. Two themes were classified as neutral risk: questions regarding campaign eligibility criteria and calls for broader HPV prevention measures.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study piloted online social listening processes to identify actionable insights into questions, concerns, and misinformation surrounding the HPV vaccination catch-up campaign among young adults. This pilot showed that online social listening can be effectively implemented even with limited resources.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform future vaccination efforts by highlighting the need to address information gaps and misinformation about HPV vaccine effectiveness and side effects. They also suggest the importance of improving communication and reducing practical barriers to vaccination.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on manually collected and coded social media data, which may introduce bias. The evidence strength is moderate, as the findings are based on a pilot study with limited resources and scope.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify actionable insights into questions, concerns, and misinformation surrounding the HPV vaccination catch-up campaign for young adults in the Netherlands. The researchers conducted a retrospective online social listening analysis across Instagram, Facebook, and X (formerly Twitter) from January 1, 2023, to June 1, 2024, using data from multiple sources. They collected and analyzed 821 posts and 5157 comments, identifying ten recurring themes across varying risk levels. High-risk themes included an information gap regarding HPV vaccination effectiveness and concerns about transparency regarding vaccine side effects. Medium-risk themes involved questioning vaccine effectiveness, reduced vaccine trust following the COVID-19 pandemic, and accessibility issues. Neutral and low-risk themes focused on eligibility criteria and scheduling. The study suggests that addressing these concerns and improving communication could enhance future vaccination efforts. However, the study is limited by its reliance on manual data collection and coding, which may introduce bias, and its moderate evidence strength due to being a pilot with limited resources.

title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus in women from northern provinces of Lao People's Democratic Republic, 2018-2019.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer is a frequent cause of morbidity and mortality in women worldwide and strongly linked to the presence of high-risk (HR) human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Between October 2018 and February 2019, a total of 1302 asymptomatic women (mean age 37.4 years, range 18-76) from Xiengkhouang, Luangprabang, Oudomxay and Huaphan provinces were invited to answer a questionnaire, and cervical cells were collected for cytology and a swab for PCR and AnyplexTM II HPV-HR detection.
analysis.methods: AnyplexTM II HPV-HR kit detected 256 positives among 1184 participants (21.6%), with types 52, 58 and 16 being the most prevalent HR genotypes (20.4%, 12.8% and 11.7%, respectively).
analysis.main_results: Overall, 114 of 1268 women with evaluable samples (9.0%) had abnormal cytology and three (0.2%) had cervical cancer.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Multivariable analysis showed that participants aged ≥ 40 years (OR: 1.6; 95% CI: 1.1-2.4, p = 0.015) and those living in Luangprabang province (OR: 1.9; 95% CI: 1.1-3.2, p = 0.02) had a higher likelihood of abnormal cytology compared to younger women and those residing in Huaphan.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: HPV 52, 58 and 16 were the most prevalent high-risk genotypes, clearly advocating for the introduction of the nonavalent vaccine.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Single/divorced/widow women had a higher probability of HPV detection compared to married women (OR: 2.3; 95% CI: 1.5-3.7, p < 0.001).

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to determine the prevalence and genotype distribution of high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) in women from northern provinces of Lao People's Democratic Republic between 2018 and 2019. A total of 1302 asymptomatic women were enrolled, and cervical cells were collected for cytology and HPV detection using PCR and AnyplexTM II HPV-HR kit. The results showed that 21.6% of participants tested positive for HPV, with types 52, 58, and 16 being the most prevalent. Overall, 9.0% of women had abnormal cytology, and 0.2% had cervical cancer. Multivariable analysis revealed that older women and those from Luangprabang province had a higher likelihood of abnormal cytology. Single/divorced/widow women were more likely to test positive for HPV compared to married women. The study highlights the importance of HPV genotypes 52, 58, and 16 in cervical cancer risk and advocates for the introduction of the nonavalent vaccine. The findings suggest that periodic screening should be considered for women too old to benefit from the vaccine.

title: Determinants of human papillomavirus vaccine uptake among ​​Iranian adults: a nationally representative survey using the Iranian HPV ​Vaccine Determinants Scale (I-HPV-VDS)

analysis.scope_and_question: The study investigates determinants of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine uptake among Iranian adults, focusing on factors influencing acceptance and coverage. The central question is to identify the key determinants of vaccine uptake and understand the current status of HPV vaccination in the population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a cross-sectional study conducted in 2025 using an online survey of Iranian adults. The study design involved psychometric assessment of the questionnaire, including face validity, construct validity, and Cronbach’s alpha. Post-stratification weighting was applied to enhance population representativeness. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify determinants of HPV vaccine uptake.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The weighted sample of 1416 Iranian adults showed an HPV vaccine uptake of 5.5%. Factors significantly associated with higher uptake included younger age, female gender, and unmarried status. Additionally, higher levels of Social Support and Self-efficacy were linked to increased odds of vaccine uptake, while Risk Perception also showed a positive association.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study notes that stigma-related and behavioral concern components were not independently associated with vaccination in multivariable analysis. The wide confidence intervals for several subgroups suggest caution in interpreting subgroup-specific findings due to low event counts and post-stratification weighting.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The critically low HPV vaccination uptake, especially among men, highlights the need for measures to improve access, such as including the HPV vaccine in the national immunization program. Strengthening public understanding of HPV susceptibility and vaccine effectiveness, along with creating supportive social environments, is essential for enhancing vaccination rates in the Iranian context.

analysis.summary_en: This review article examines the determinants of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine uptake among Iranian adults, using a nationally representative survey. The study highlights that uptake is low, with only 5.5% of the weighted sample vaccinated. Key factors associated with higher uptake include younger age, female gender, and unmarried status. Social support, self-efficacy, and risk perception also positively influence vaccine acceptance. However, stigma-related and behavioral concerns were not independently linked to vaccination. The findings emphasize the need for targeted public health interventions to improve access and awareness, particularly in addressing gender disparities and social inequities in HPV vaccination rates.

title: Cervical cancer risk reduction in the era of human papillomavirus vaccination.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the population-level impact of cervical screening uptake on cervical cancer risk in relation to HPV vaccination status, as screening rates are rarely presented by vaccination status, limiting assessments of population-level protection against cervical cancer.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used data from the 2019 National Health Interview Survey, including 4000 females aged 21–39 years, to report the proportion up-to-date with cervical screening stratified by age and self-reported HPV vaccination status.
analysis.methods: The authors analyzed data from the 2019 National Health Interview Survey to report the proportion of females up-to-date with cervical screening, stratified by age and self-reported HPV vaccination status. They used assumptions of 85% and 70% reduction in cervical cancer risk from HPV vaccination and up-to-date screening status, respectively, to explore population-level risk reduction.
analysis.main_results: Results showed that 78.4% of females were up-to-date with screening, 38.0% reported ever receiving an HPV vaccine, and 15.3% were both unvaccinated and not up-to-date with screening. Across age groups, the proportion of females up-to-date with screening was 6.3%–19.1% higher for vaccinated versus unvaccinated females.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that cervical screening rates are higher among females who were vaccinated against HPV, resulting in a higher population-level risk of cervical cancer than expected from considering vaccination and screening rates independently.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that integrating vaccination status into national surveillance data sets could help identify and target interventions within communities at higher risk, thereby improving cervical cancer prevention strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on self-reported data and does not account for potential biases or confounding factors. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on survey data rather than direct clinical or biological measurements.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the relationship between HPV vaccination status and cervical screening uptake in females aged 21–39 years, using data from the 2019 National Health Interview Survey. It highlights that cervical screening rates are higher among vaccinated females, leading to a higher population-level risk of cervical cancer than anticipated. The authors explore the combined impact of vaccination and screening on reducing cervical cancer risk, noting that vaccinated females had higher screening uptake across age groups. They emphasize the importance of including vaccination status in surveillance data to better target interventions in high-risk communities. The study's findings are based on survey data and assumptions about risk reduction, which may introduce limitations. The evidence is considered moderate due to the reliance on self-reported information and the absence of direct biological measurements.

title: CRISPR/Cas-Enabled Point-of-Care Screening of Human Papillomavirus in Cervical Cancer

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on Human papillomaviruses (HPV), particularly high-risk subtypes, as the primary pathogen associated with cervical cancer. The central question is the evaluation of CRISPR/Cas-enabled technologies for point-of-care (POC) detection of HPV, with an emphasis on their utility in diagnosing HPV-related diseases such as cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and HPV-associated cervical cancer.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic evaluation of HPV biomarkers, including DNA, RNA, and proteins, with a focus on CRISPR/Cas-based technologies for POC detection. It discusses the performance of diverse CRISPR/Cas systems for multiplex biomarker detection in POC settings and explores signal-enhancement strategies to balance accuracy and practicality.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that CRISPR/Cas-based biosensors have emerged as transformative tools for POC testing due to their exceptional specificity and programmable cleavage activity. It highlights the potential of these technologies for rapid, accessible HPV screening in clinical settings, particularly for high-risk subtypes associated with cervical cancer.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies limitations in the current evidence, including the need for further validation of CRISPR/Cas systems in diverse POC settings and the lack of standardized protocols for signal readout. It also notes the absence of comprehensive data on the performance of these technologies in low-resource environments.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review proposes a roadmap for clinical translation, emphasizing the integration of AI-assisted platforms to enhance multiplexed detection capabilities. It suggests future research priorities in developing more robust, user-friendly POC systems and improving their applicability in decentralized healthcare settings.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates CRISPR/Cas-based biosensors for point-of-care (POC) detection of human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly high-risk subtypes linked to cervical cancer. It highlights the potential of these technologies to improve rapid and accessible HPV screening, while addressing limitations such as the need for standardized protocols and validation in diverse settings. The review also proposes the use of AI-assisted platforms to advance multiplexed detection and support decentralized HPV screening, contributing to the global elimination of cervical cancer.

title: Knowledge gaps in human papillomavirus infection and vaccination among Polish medical students: an item-level cross-sectional analysis with an embedded feasibility evaluation of a multidisciplinary educational webinar

analysis.research_question_and_background: Poland introduced universal adolescent human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination only in June 2023, and coverage remains low. Because clinicians' recommendations strongly influence uptake, future physicians' preparedness matters.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a cross-sectional knowledge assessment with an embedded single-arm pre–post feasibility component conducted at the University of Zielona Góra, Poland, in February 2024. All 96 fourth-year medical students, none of whom had begun the infectious-diseases course, were invited to a voluntary five-hour expert-led webinar.
analysis.methods: A 20-item single-choice questionnaire was administered immediately before and after the webinar. The primary outcome was item difficulty; analyses comprised Wilson 95% confidence intervals, corrected item–total correlations, Kuder–Richardson Formula 20 (KR-20) with KR-20-if-item-deleted, and McNemar's exact test with Bonferroni–Holm correction.
analysis.main_results: Fifty-four of 96 invited students (56.2%) provided complete paired data: 37 women, 17 men. The mean baseline score was 13.19/20 (SD 3.76); KR-20 0.79. Performance varied more than fivefold across items (18.5–98.1%), so the mean concealed the educationally relevant pattern. Four items were answered correctly by half the cohort or fewer: cervical cancer as an uncommon individual outcome of infection (18.5%), the cervical cancer burden in Ukraine (20.4%), the vaccines' registered age (35.2%) and adult schedules (50.0%). All 54 subsequently scored 20/20, but this ceiling, on an immediate unproctored post-test, is uninterpretable as learning.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Deficits concentrated in the applied and epidemiological content of HPV prevention - eligibility, age indications, dose schedules and individual cancer risk after infection not in the biology of the virus or its vaccines. The module was feasible to deliver and evaluate; controlled studies with proctored, delayed assessment are needed before claiming effectiveness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for targeted educational interventions to address knowledge gaps in HPV prevention, particularly regarding epidemiological and applied aspects. They also highlight the importance of evaluating educational modules for effectiveness before implementation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its cross-sectional design and the lack of proctored, delayed assessment to determine learning effectiveness. The evidence is moderate as it provides insights into knowledge gaps but does not establish causality or long-term impact.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the baseline knowledge of HPV among Polish fourth-year medical students and evaluated the feasibility of an educational webinar. It found significant gaps in understanding applied aspects of HPV prevention, such as eligibility, age indications, and individual cancer risk after infection, while virology and vaccine science knowledge was stronger. The study highlights the need for targeted educational interventions and controlled studies with proctored assessments to evaluate learning effectiveness. The findings suggest that future physicians require improved training in HPV-related public health measures to support vaccination uptake and clinical decision-making.

title: Human Papillomavirus Testing Compared With Cytology for Cervical Cancer Screening Among Women Living With HIV in the Dominican Republic.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Women living with HIV (WWH) face elevated cervical cancer risk, yet evidence supporting primary human papillomavirus (HPV) testing in low-resource settings remains limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We compared HPV testing with cytology for detection of cervical precancer among WWH in the Dominican Republic to inform national screening strategies.
analysis.methods: In this cross-sectional analysis from US-Latin American-Caribbean HIV/HPV-Cancer Prevention Clinical Trials Network Trial 302 (Estudio Oportunidad, ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05556772), 575 WWH contributed provider- and self-collected samples for cytology and HPV hierarchical testing.
analysis.main_results: Women with positive results on any screening test had higher HIV viral loads, lower CD4 counts, and were younger than women with screen-negative results.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Sensitivity to detect cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN3+) by cytology (66.7% [95% CI, 49.2 to 80.5]) was lower than sensitivity of provider-collected results with either 13 high-risk HPV (hrHPV) genotypes (93.9 [95% CI, 78.7 to 98.5]) or 8 hrHPV genotypes (84.8% [95% CI, 68.3 to 98.6]).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Among WWH in the Dominican Republic, HPV testing, whether provider- or self-collected, outperformed cytology for detection of CIN3+.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: These findings support transitioning to primary HPV-based screening for WWH in the Dominican Republic to increase accuracy in detecting precancer and reduce the cervical cancer burden among WWH.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of HPV testing compared to cytology for detecting cervical precancer in women living with HIV (WWH) in the Dominican Republic. The research aimed to inform national screening strategies by comparing these methods in a cross-sectional analysis. The study included 575 WWH who provided provider- and self-collected samples for testing. Results showed that HPV testing, particularly with self-collected samples, had higher sensitivity for detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN3+) than cytology. The findings suggest that transitioning to primary HPV-based screening could improve detection accuracy and reduce cervical cancer burden among WWH. However, both 13- and 8-genotype HPV panels had high sensitivity but low specificity, leading to high referral rates for colposcopy. The study's evidence is strong, but limitations include the cross-sectional design and potential biases in sample collection and interpretation.

title: Study on the molecular mechanism of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells inducing epithelial-mesenchymal transition in HPV-associated cervical cancer through activation of miR-129.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the role of miR-129 in HPV-associated cervical cancer, addressing the unclear relationship between miR-129 and tumor progression.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved 77 cervical cancer and 30 normal cervical tissue samples, with BMSCs co-cultured with SiHa and HeLa cells.
analysis.methods: miR-129 expression was measured by qRT-PCR, and associations with clinicopathological features and OS were analyzed. BMSCs were co-cultured with SiHa and HeLa cells, and cell proliferation, invasion, and expression of E-cadherin, N-cadherin, and MRP1 were examined.
analysis.main_results: miR-129 was significantly upregulated in cervical cancer tissues compared to normal controls. High miR-129 expression correlated with tumor size, FIGO stage, and lymph node metastasis, and was associated with shorter OS. BMSC co-culture upregulated miR-129, promoting proliferation, colony formation, and invasion, while miR-129 knockdown suppressed these phenotypes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study suggests that miR-129 may contribute to cervical cancer progression, but further in-vivo and mechanistic studies are needed.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: miR-129 shows potential as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for HPV-associated cervical cancer, and the BMSCs/miR-129 axis may contribute to cervical cancer progression.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of in vitro models and the need for further in-vivo validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated miR-129 expression in HPV-associated cervical cancer and found it to be significantly upregulated, correlating with tumor progression and prognosis. BMSCs upregulated miR-129, promoting cancer cell proliferation and invasion, suggesting a role in cervical cancer progression.

title: Human Papillomavirus-Associated Papillomatous Lesions of the Oral Mucosa: A Narrative Review of Clinical, Histopathological, and Genotype-Specific Features

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on human papillomaviruses (HPV) and their association with papillomatous lesions in the oral mucosa. It examines the clinical, histopathological, and genotype-specific features of these lesions, with an emphasis on HPV types and their role in disease progression. The central question is whether HPV-associated oral epithelial dysplasia represents a distinct potentially malignant entity and how different HPV genotypes contribute to various oral lesions.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of clinical, histopathological, and molecular evidence. It grades each primary study based on the level of viral evidence it provides, ranging from clinical diagnosis to transcriptionally active infection. The review does not perform a meta-analysis but instead provides a qualitative summary of findings from the literature.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that HPV 6 and 11 are predominantly associated with condylomas and squamous papillomas, while HPV 13 and 32 are linked to multifocal epithelial hyperplasia. However, the association of HPV 2 and 4 with oral verruca vulgaris is based on limited studies. Additionally, HPV-associated oral epithelial dysplasia is considered a distinct potentially malignant entity, though its frequency and transformation risk remain uncertain.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is controversy regarding the use of markers such as koilocytosis, papillary architecture, p16 expression, and HPV DNA detection to establish causation. The review also highlights that evidence from oropharyngeal carcinoma cannot be directly extended to the oral cavity. Furthermore, the frequency and transformation risk of HPV-associated oral epithelial dysplasia are not well established, indicating a significant evidence gap.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review proposes lesion-specific indications for supplementary HPV testing and emphasizes the need to distinguish between well-supported conclusions and those that remain uncertain. It suggests that further research is required to clarify the role of specific HPV genotypes in oral lesions and to better understand the transformation risk of HPV-associated oral epithelial dysplasia.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review explores the role of human papillomaviruses (HPV) in oral papillomatous lesions, focusing on clinical, histopathological, and molecular features. It highlights the predominant association of HPV 6 and 11 with condylomas and squamous papillomas, while noting the limited evidence for HPV 2 and 4 in oral verruca vulgaris. The review identifies HPV-associated oral epithelial dysplasia as a potentially malignant entity, though its frequency and transformation risk are uncertain. It also cautions against using single markers like koilocytosis or p16 expression to establish causation and stresses the need for targeted HPV testing. The findings suggest that further research is necessary to clarify the pathogenic roles of specific HPV genotypes in oral lesions and to improve diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.

title: The Neuroimmune Signature Underlying HPV Infection and Cervical Cancer Progression

analysis.research_question_and_background: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) is the principal cause of cervical cancer, yet the multicellular signalling programmes that accompany disease progression remain incompletely defined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, we integrated Single cell RNA sequencing, independent microarray and bulk RNA-sequencing meta analyses, and TCGA CESC tumor data to characterize the neuroimmune transcriptional architecture of HPV associated cervical disease.
analysis.methods: Single cell profiling revealed progressive remodeling of epithelial, stromal, endothelial and immune compartments across HPV infection, high grade squamous intraepithelial lesions and cervical cancer.
analysis.main_results: Although immune dysregulation predominated, lesion and tumor states showed coordinated enrichment of nervous system associated programs, including synapse organization, trans-synaptic signaling, axon development, neurogenesis and neurotransmitter-related signaling.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These programs formed interconnected networks with cytokine production, leukocyte activation, chemotaxis, cell adhesion, apoptosis, and immune effector regulation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Cross-platform integration identified a recurrent 12-gene neuroimmune signature associated with tumor grade related transcriptional variation, including CXCL12, P2RY6, P2RX5 and TACR1.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Ligand receptor inference further highlighted glutamatergic, adrenergic, noradrenergic, GABAergic and purinergic signaling circuits.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to understand the neuroimmune signaling programs associated with HPV infection and cervical cancer progression. The researchers integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, microarray, and bulk RNA-sequencing data from TCGA CESC tumor samples to characterize the neuroimmune transcriptional architecture of HPV-associated cervical disease. Their findings revealed progressive remodeling of multiple cellular compartments, including immune, epithelial, stromal, and endothelial, across different stages of HPV infection and cervical cancer. The study identified a 12-gene neuroimmune signature linked to tumor grade, highlighting key genes such as CXCL12, P2RY6, P2RX5, and TACR1. Additionally, ligand receptor inference uncovered various signaling circuits, including glutamatergic, adrenergic, noradrenergic, GABAergic, and purinergic, distributed across multiple cell types rather than confined to a canonical neural compartment. These results define cervical carcinogenesis as a distributed neuroimmune state, potentially offering new biomarkers and therapeutic targets. The study's evidence is strong, but its abstract-only nature limits the depth of analysis.

title: A Community Engaged Feasibility Study of High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Self-Sampling for Cervical Cancer Screening in Sexual and Gender Minority People

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the acceptability and feasibility of at-home self-sampling cervical cancer screening (CCS) for high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) in sexual and gender minority (SGM) Kentuckians.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A descriptive qualitative study was conducted using virtual interviews with 19 participants in 2022–2023 to explore socioecological factors influencing cervical cancer screening and the feasibility of hrHPV self-sampling in SGM individuals.
analysis.methods: Criterion and snowball sampling were used to recruit participants, and data were analyzed using a hybrid inductive-deductive thematic approach with team member consensus to identify salient themes.
analysis.main_results: Nineteen participants completed hrHPV self-sampling and qualitative interviews, and six overarching themes were identified related to cervical cancer screening perceptions, prior negative healthcare experiences, desirability of hrHPV self-sampling, completing hrHPV self-sampling, concerns about hrHPV self-sampling, and reasons for study participation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that at-home hrHPV self-sampling is a promising intervention to increase cervical cancer screening in SGM people, highlighting the need for healthcare providers to be affirming and culturally competent partners.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that hrHPV self-sampling could be a valuable tool for improving cervical cancer screening rates among SGM individuals, potentially contributing to more equitable healthcare access and outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its qualitative design and small sample size, but the evidence is strong given the thorough thematic analysis and team member consensus.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the acceptability and feasibility of at-home self-sampling cervical cancer screening (CCS) for high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) among sexual and gender minority (SGM) Kentuckians. Using virtual interviews with 19 participants, the research explored socioecological factors influencing CCS and the feasibility of hrHPV self-sampling. Six overarching themes emerged, including perceptions of cervical cancer screening, prior negative healthcare experiences, and the desirability of self-sampling. The authors concluded that at-home hrHPV self-sampling is a promising intervention to increase CCS in SGM individuals, emphasizing the need for healthcare providers to be affirming and culturally competent. The study's qualitative design and small sample size limit its generalizability, but the thematic analysis and team consensus provide strong evidence for the potential of hrHPV self-sampling in this population.

title: Buschke-Löwenstein Tumor Spectrum Giant Condyloma with Mixed High- and Low-Risk Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Coinfection in an Adolescent with Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia (AIHA): A Case Report.

analysis.scope_and_question: Buschke-Löwenstein tumor (BLT), or giant condyloma acuminatum (GCA) is a rare, locally aggressive HPV-associated anogenital lesion characterized by extensive verrucous proliferation and a recognized potential for malignant transformation. To report a rare case of BLT-spectrum giant condyloma in an adolescent girl with autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) and mixed HPV 11, 16, and 18 coinfection, and to discuss the associated diagnostic challenges and potential oncogenic risk from a low resource setting perspective.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: CASE REPORT: A 16-year-old HIV-negative, unmarried adolescent presented with a progressively enlarging vulvar mass over 8 months, with marked growth over the preceding two months.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Histopathology showed papillomatous hyperplastic stratified squamous epithelium with marked acanthosis, hyperkeratosis, elongated rete ridges, and prominent koilocytotic changes, consistent with HPV-associated cytopathic effects, without stromal invasion or malignant transformation. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated increased Ki-67 proliferative activity, patchy (non-block) p16, and wild-type p53, consistent with a productive HPV-associated lesion without immunophenotypic evidence of transcriptionally active high-risk HPV or invasive carcinoma. HPV genotyping detected HPV 11, 16, and 18, whereas HPV 6 was negative.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: These conclusions are based on a single case and should be interpreted accordingly.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Despite benign histopathology, coexistence of high-risk HPV genotypes, rapid growth, and immunological impairment warrants cautious interpretation regarding potential premalignant risk and underscores the importance of adequate tissue sampling, long-term surveillance, and HPV prevention.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a rare instance of Buschke-Löwenstein tumor (BLT)-spectrum giant condyloma in an adolescent girl with autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) and mixed HPV 11, 16, and 18 coinfection. The patient presented with a progressively enlarging vulvar mass, and histopathology and immunohistochemistry confirmed the presence of HPV-associated cytopathic effects without evidence of malignant transformation. The case highlights the diagnostic challenges and potential oncogenic risk associated with mixed HPV infections in immunocompromised individuals. The findings emphasize the need for thorough tissue sampling, long-term surveillance, and HPV prevention strategies, particularly in low-resource settings. However, the conclusions are limited to a single case and should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Multiple Extraintestinal Malignancies and HPV16-Associated Neoplasms in Crohn’s Disease Under Prolonged Immunosuppression: A Case Report

analysis.research_question_and_background: Crohn’s disease (CD) is a chronic inflammatory disease of the gastrointestinal tract with an increased risk for malignancy, particularly in patients undergoing immunosuppressive therapy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This report describes the 23-year clinical course of a 20-year-old woman diagnosed with CD who, under prolonged therapy with azathioprine (AZA), developed three distinct carcinomas.
analysis.methods: High-risk HPV16 DNA was detected in cervical and conjunctival malignancies by PCR and confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Immunohistochemical analysis showed high Ki-67 and p16 expression and CD4+ cell predominance, supporting an association of HPV16 in these neoplasms.
analysis.main_results: After CD recurrence and AZA resumption, CIN 2 was detected (Year 18; ~10.2 cumulative years of AZA). Within less than one year (Year 19), cervical squamous cell carcinoma was diagnosed. In Year 23, CD was controlled, without neoplasms documented.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This case highlights the temporal co-occurrence of Crohn’s disease, prolonged immunosuppression, and HPV16 infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings raise the need for vigilant extraintestinal cancer surveillance, regular screening, and HPV vaccination during chronic immunosuppression.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The short interval between CIN 2 and invasive CSCC detection is unusual. While this coincided with chronic immunosuppression, direct causality currently cannot be inferred; however, the patient’s chronic immune dysregulation and immunosuppression may be contributing factors.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 20-year-old woman with Crohn’s disease who developed multiple extraintestinal malignancies, including cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN 1, 2) and cervical squamous cell carcinoma, while undergoing prolonged azathioprine therapy. HPV16 was detected in the cervical and conjunctival malignancies through PCR and Sanger sequencing, with immunohistochemical analysis showing high Ki-67 and p16 expression. The case highlights the potential association between prolonged immunosuppression, CD, and HPV16 infection, suggesting the need for increased cancer surveillance and HPV vaccination in immunosuppressed patients. However, the authors note that direct causality cannot be inferred, and the patient’s immune dysregulation may be a contributing factor. The study provides a unique clinical example of the co-occurrence of these conditions but is limited by its observational nature and lack of controlled comparisons.

title: Comparative Evaluation of E6/E7 mRNA Expression and Viral DNA Load in Cervical Lesions With Multiple High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Infection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Multiple high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infections are frequently detected in cervical screening, but their biological interactions and clinical significance remain unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Among 12 000 cervical specimens tested for hrHPV, 598 were positive and 72 showed multiple genotypes. A tissue-available subset of 36 dual HPV16 + 52 or HPV16 + 58 cases was analyzed by duplex RNAscope for genotype-specific E6/E7 mRNA expression and localization.
analysis.methods: Viral load was assessed using the BioPerfectus Multiplex Real-Time assay. Diagnoses were categorized as benign, low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL), or high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL). Viral load and RNAscope analyses used incompletely matched subsets and were interpreted as complementary, not paired.
analysis.main_results: Elevated viral load (≥4.00 log10 copies/10 000 cells) was associated with HSIL. In cohort-level analyses, diffuse (+++) E6/E7 mRNA expression was more frequent in HSIL than elevated viral load (95.2% vs 55.5%, P = .01). RNAscope-negative cases were mostly benign or LSIL and showed no progression. Genotype-specific signals were spatially distinct, with rare overlap. Dual-positive cells showed fewer RNA signals than adjacent single-positive cells (P < .001). Higher E6/E7 mRNA expression showed possible association with LSIL progression, but events were limited.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In multiplex hrHPV infection, transcriptional activity may better reflect cervical lesion biology than viral DNA burden alone. Genotype-specific E6/E7 mRNA expression may complement HPV DNA load.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that E6/E7 mRNA expression could provide additional insights into the progression of cervical lesions associated with multiple hrHPV infections, potentially improving diagnostic and prognostic approaches.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study used incompletely matched subsets for viral load and RNAscope analyses, which may limit the strength of the association observed. The evidence is moderate due to the exploratory nature and potential for confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between E6/E7 mRNA expression and viral DNA load in cervical lesions with multiple high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infections. It analyzed 12,000 cervical specimens, identifying 598 hrHPV-positive cases and 72 with multiple genotypes. A subset of 36 dual HPV16 + 52 or HPV16 + 58 cases was examined using duplex RNAscope to assess mRNA expression and localization. Results showed that elevated viral load was associated with high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL), while diffuse E6/E7 mRNA expression was more frequent in HSIL than in elevated viral load. title: High-risk HPV integration reprograms cis-regulatory architecture through HPV-specific stripe transcription factors

analysis.research_question_and_background: The integration of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) DNA into the host genome contributes to persistent viral infection and malignant progression in hrHPV-related carcinomas, but the integration-associated cis-regulatory programs remain incompletely defined, limiting the identification of potential therapeutic vulnerabilities.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Human cervical epithelial organoids carrying integrated HPV16 upstream regulatory region-E6/E7 sequences and an HPV16-integrated mouse model (14 E2.2 HPV16-int) were established to assess integration-associated regulatory changes and pharmacological perturbation.
analysis.methods: Viral integration mapping, motif enrichment analysis, chromatin accessibility and histone modification profiling, three-dimensional chromatin interaction analysis, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, and patient-derived organoid/xenograft models were integrated to evaluate the regulatory changes associated with hrHPV integration.
analysis.main_results: Human epithelial organoids and mice with hrHPV integration recapitulated progressive malignant phenotypes in vitro and in vivo. Across cervical and head and neck cancer datasets, hrHPV integration hotspots were enriched for motifs of a defined subset of 25 HPV-specific stripe transcription factors (HSTFs). Higher HSTF motif density was associated with increased chromatin accessibility, active histone marks, enhanced super-enhancer-promoter interactions, and elevated HSTF regulatory activity along hrHPV-positive epithelial cancer trajectories.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings reveal an hrHPV integration-associated cis-regulatory network that promotes chromatin remodeling and transcriptional activation in HPV-driven carcinogenesis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Targeting HSTF-associated regulatory programs may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for hrHPV-integrated precancerous lesions and cancers.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on preclinical models and does not include human clinical trials, which limits the direct applicability of findings to human populations. The evidence is moderate due to the reliance on in vitro and in vivo models.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) integration reprograms cis-regulatory architecture through HPV-specific stripe transcription factors (HSTFs). The research aimed to characterize the regulatory changes associated with hrHPV integration and evaluate their functional relevance in preclinical models. Using a combination of viral integration mapping, chromatin profiling, transcriptomics, and spatial analyses, the study found that hrHPV integration hotspots are enriched for HSTF motifs, which correlate with increased chromatin accessibility, active histone marks, and enhanced transcriptional activity in cancer progression. These results suggest that HSTFs play a critical role in HPV-driven carcinogenesis and that targeting their regulatory programs could offer new therapeutic strategies for hrHPV-related cancers. However, the study's reliance on preclinical models limits the direct translation of findings to human populations, resulting in moderate confidence in the evidence.

title: Presence of HPV infection, not age, identifies vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia: a 847-patient multivariable analysis with 40- and 45-year age-cutoff sensitivity testing

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to determine whether HPV infection or age is more strongly associated with vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN), as VIN is a precursor of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma with two biologically distinct pathways: HPV-associated and HPV-independent disease.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A multivariable analysis was conducted on 847 women referred for colposcopy and vulvar evaluation between April 2022 and December 2025, including 568 VIN patients and 279 non-VIN controls.
analysis.methods: Univariable comparisons, age-stratified multivariable logistic regression (Enter method; complete-case n = 673), and sensitivity analyses using 40-year and 45-year cutoffs were performed to assess the association between age, HPV infection, and VIN.
analysis.main_results: Univariable analysis showed VIN patients were slightly younger (mean 39.66 ± 11.95 vs. 41.51 ± 12.52 years), more frequently asymptomatic, and had a higher HPV infection rate (80.2% vs. 55.7%, both P < 0.05 at 40-year and 45-year cutoffs).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The marginal statistical significance of continuous age in the primary model reflects residual confounding by HPV infection and multifocal disease accumulation rather than an independent pathogenic role of chronological age.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that vulvar inspection should be guided by HPV infection status and concurrent lower genital tract neoplasia rather than arbitrary age cutoffs, particularly given the high prevalence of asymptomatic VIN.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's design, which included univariable comparisons and multivariable logistic regression, may have limitations in controlling for all confounding factors, but the evidence is strong given the consistent and independent association of HPV infection with VIN across all models.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between HPV infection and age with vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN), a precursor to vulvar squamous cell carcinoma. It analyzed 847 women, including 568 VIN patients and 279 non-VIN controls, using univariable comparisons, multivariable logistic regression, and sensitivity analyses with age cutoffs. The results showed VIN patients were younger and had a higher HPV infection rate compared to non-VIN controls. The marginal significance of age was attributed to residual confounding by HPV infection and multifocal disease. The study concluded that VIN should be identified by HPV infection status rather than age, emphasizing the need for HPV-focused screening. The findings have implications for clinical practice, suggesting that vulvar inspections should prioritize HPV testing and concurrent lower genital tract neoplasia detection over age-based criteria. The evidence is strong, but the study's design may limit its ability to fully control for confounding factors.

title: Enhancing Human Papillomavirus Vaccine Communication with Mobile Health: Usability Insights from Caregivers and Health Care Providers.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the suboptimal uptake of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine, especially among rural and underserved populations, by evaluating the usability of a newly developed mHealth app compared to the CDC's HPV vaccine Web site.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A mixed-methods design was used, involving caregivers and health care providers who were randomized to use both the CDC Web site and the mHealth app in alternating order.
analysis.methods: The study employed the Health Belief Model and the mHealth Agile Development and Evaluation Lifecycle, using quantitative and qualitative methods to assess usability, acceptability, and perceived usefulness.
analysis.main_results: Quantitative results indicated no difference in ease of use or effort required between the tools, while qualitative feedback highlighted the app's streamlined navigation and tailored content.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that tailored mHealth tools may better meet the informational and usability needs of caregivers and health care providers compared to existing web-based resources, supporting further development of such tools.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that mHealth tools can enhance HPV vaccine communication, potentially improving vaccine uptake, particularly among underserved populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include its reliance on self-reported measures and the potential for bias in the randomization process, which may affect the generalizability of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the usability of a newly developed mHealth app for HPV vaccine communication compared to the CDC's Web site, finding that the app may better meet the informational and usability needs of caregivers and health care providers, supporting further development of such tools to enhance vaccine communication.

title: Presence of Human Papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr Virus in Breast Cancer Biopsies as Potential Risk Factors

analysis.research_question_and_background: Breast cancer represents the leading cause of cancer-related death in the Venezuelan female population. Many risk factors favoring its appearance have been reported; however, human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus have been associated in the past few decades as potential risk factors in the development of this malignancy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Fresh biopsies were collected from patients with breast cancer and patients with breast benign pathology attending the Hospital Universitario de Caracas for surgery.
analysis.methods: Human papillomavirus detection was made using the INNO-LIPA ® HPV Genotyping Extra commercial kit (Innogenetics), and Epstein-Barr virus genome was detected with Epstein-Barr Virus BMLF1 commercial kit (Maxim Biotech, Inc.).
analysis.main_results: 63.6 and 13.6% of breast cancer cases were positive for human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus DNA, respectively, whereas the benign pathology samples had 4.5% positivity for each one of the viruses; 42.90% of breast cancer samples had mixed infection with low and high oncogenic risk human papillomavirus genotypes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: We can suggest that human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus are important risk factors for breast cancer.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform future studies on the role of human papillomavirus in breast cancer development and highlight the need for further investigation into its potential as a risk factor.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the presence of human papillomavirus (HPV) and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) in breast cancer biopsies to determine their potential role as risk factors. The research is motivated by the fact that breast cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death in Venezuelan women, and previous associations between HPV and EBV and breast cancer have been noted. The study collected fresh biopsies from patients with breast cancer and those with benign pathology at the Hospital Universitario de Caracas. HPV was detected using the INNO-LIPA ® HPV Genotyping Extra commercial kit, while EBV was identified with the Epstein-Barr Virus BMLF1 commercial kit. Results showed that 63.6% of breast cancer cases were positive for HPV DNA, and 13.6% for EBV DNA, compared to 4.5% for each virus in benign samples. Additionally, 42.90% of breast cancer samples had mixed infections with low and high oncogenic risk HPV genotypes. The authors suggest that HPV and EBV may be important risk factors for breast cancer, though further studies are needed to clarify their role. The study's findings are limited by the lack of detailed limitations or evidence strength assessment.

title: Post-Treatment Surveillance After Conisation for CIN2/3 in Norway: Long-Term CIN3+ Risk Stratification Comparing HPV DNA Testing with Cytology/HPV16/18/45 mRNA Co-Testing

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of different post-treatment surveillance strategies for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2/3 (CIN2/3) in identifying long-term CIN3+ risk, addressing the need for improved risk stratification methods after conisation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective regional cohort of 2136 women who underwent conisation for CIN2/3 between 2016 and 2020 was studied. Histological outcomes were ascertained through 2025, with median administrative follow-up of 7.24 years.
analysis.methods: The study evaluated cytology, HPV DNA testing, and HPV16/18/45 E6/E7 mRNA co-testing, individually and in combination, using results from the first eligible visit 90–548 days after treatment. An exploratory referral strategy adapted from the ATHENA study was also assessed.
analysis.main_results: CIN3+ was recorded in 74 women (3.5%). HPV DNA testing had 93.2% sensitivity, 78.0% specificity, and 24.4% positivity. Combining ASC-US+ cytology with mRNA positivity achieved the highest observed CIN3+ sensitivity (95.9%) with 73.5% specificity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that cytology and genotype-specific mRNA co-testing may support risk stratification after conisation, offering a more sensitive approach for detecting CIN3+.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform the development of more effective surveillance strategies for cervical cancer risk after treatment, potentially improving long-term monitoring and reducing the risk of missed diagnoses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and lacks prospective evaluation, which limits confidence in the proposed surveillance intervals. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature and potential for bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated post-treatment surveillance strategies for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2/3 (CIN2/3) in a regional cohort of 2136 women in Norway. The primary aim was to assess the effectiveness of HPV DNA testing, cytology, and HPV16/18/45 E6/E7 mRNA co-testing in identifying long-term CIN3+ risk. Results showed that HPV DNA testing had 93.2% sensitivity and 78.0% specificity, while combining ASC-US+ cytology with mRNA positivity achieved the highest observed sensitivity (95.9%) with 73.5% specificity. The authors suggest that cytology and genotype-specific mRNA co-testing may support improved risk stratification after conisation. However, the study is retrospective and lacks prospective evaluation, which limits confidence in the proposed surveillance intervals. The findings may inform more effective long-term monitoring strategies for cervical cancer risk post-treatment.

title: Factors associated with biopsy-confirmed high-grade cervical lesions (CIN2+) in women undergoing colposcopy: role of HPV infection, vaccination status, and cytology

analysis.research_question_and_background: Background High-grade cervical lesions (CIN2+) are important precursors of cervical cancer. This study aimed to evaluate factors associated with biopsy-confirmed CIN2+ in women undergoing colposcopy, with particular focus on HPV infection and vaccination status.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 246 women undergoing colposcopy from January 2014 to January 2024. The study focused on women with biopsy-confirmed CIN2+ and compared them with those without such lesions.
analysis.methods: HPV status, vaccination status, cytology, and clinical characteristics were assessed. Univariable and multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with CIN2+.
analysis.main_results: Among 246 women included in the analysis, 50 (20.3%) had biopsy-confirmed CIN2+, including 37 (74.0%) with CIN2, 10 (20.0%) with CIN3, 2 (4.0%) with adenocarcinoma in situ, and 1 (2.0%) with invasive cervical cancer. HPV status and cytological findings differed significantly between women with CIN2+ and CIN2− (both p < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression, HPV16/18 infection (aOR, 3.94; 95% CI, 1.70–9.74; p = 0.001), lack of HPV vaccination (aOR, 2.20; 95% CI, 1.03–4.65; p = 0.042), and HSIL cytology compared with NILM (aOR, 2.84; 95% CI, 1.09–7.54; p = 0.031) were independently associated with CIN2+.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that HPV16/18 infection and HSIL cytology are important factors in the development of CIN2+. This information can inform cervical cancer screening and prevention strategies, particularly in populations where HPV vaccination rates are low.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The timing of vaccination relative to HPV exposure was not recorded, and the association with lack of HPV vaccination may reflect unmeasured confounding parameters. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated factors associated with biopsy-confirmed high-grade cervical lesions (CIN2+) in women undergoing colposcopy, focusing on HPV infection, vaccination status, and cytology. A retrospective cross-sectional design was used, including 246 women from 2014 to 2024. HPV status, vaccination status, cytology, and clinical characteristics were assessed using Firth penalized logistic regression. Among the participants, 20.3% had CIN2+, with HPV16/18 infection, lack of HPV vaccination, and HSIL cytology independently associated with CIN2+. The study highlights the importance of HPV16/18 and HSIL in CIN2+ development, but the association with vaccination status requires cautious interpretation due to unrecorded vaccination timing and potential confounding. The findings have implications for cervical cancer prevention and screening, particularly in populations with low vaccination rates.
